learn_buttons.label: Yellow (round)
learn_buttons.note: Yellow antenna; from 2022 some carry a Step Saver label (315 or 390 MHz)

learn_buttons.label: Blue (replacement board)
learn_buttons.note: Replacement logic board with alternate frequency; discontinued

learn_buttons.label: Genie Intellicode (square PROGRAM/SET or round LEARN CODE button)
learn_buttons.note: Current openers: square PRGM/SET button with blue/purple LEDs. Older Intellicode openers: round LEARN CODE button with red LED; 1995-1997 openers use specific remote buttons.

learn_buttons.label: Code switches (pre-Intellicode)
learn_buttons.note: Genie lists these as not compatible with Chamberlain universal accessories: Alliance, BlueMax, Crytar, Hercules, Medallion and others.

openers.learn_button_basis: manual names Security+ 2.0
openers.learn_button_location: On the back or side panel of the motor unit, close to where the antenna wire hangs down.
openers.homelink_bridge_note: Many cars built before about 2012 need a HomeLink repeater/bridge (e.g. 855LM) for Security+ 2.0 openers.

remote: Find the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Press and release LEARN; its LED stays lit for about 30 seconds.
Within those 30 seconds, press and hold the remote button you want to use.
Let go when the opener lights blink or you hear two clicks.
Press the remote button again to test.
keypad: Press and release the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Within 30 seconds, type a 4-digit PIN of your choice on the keypad.
Press and hold ENTER until the opener lights blink or you hear two clicks.
Enter the PIN and press ENTER to test.
car: Program the HomeLink button with your remote first (see your vehicle's steps).
Press and release the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Within 30 seconds, press and hold the programmed HomeLink button for 2 seconds, then release.
Repeat up to 3 times until the door moves.
erase: Press and hold the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Keep holding for about 6 seconds until the LEARN LED goes out.
All remotes and keypads are now erased; reprogram the ones you want to keep.

openers.homelink_bridge_note: Many cars built before about 2012 need a HomeLink repeater/bridge (e.g. 855LM) for Security+ 2.0 openers.

remote: Find the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Press and release LEARN; its LED stays lit for about 30 seconds.
Within those 30 seconds, press and hold the remote button you want to use.
Let go when the opener lights blink or you hear two clicks.
Press the remote button again to test.
keypad: Press and release the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Within 30 seconds, type a 4-digit PIN of your choice on the keypad.
Press and hold ENTER until the opener lights blink or you hear two clicks.
Enter the PIN and press ENTER to test.
car: Program the HomeLink button with your remote first (see your vehicle's steps).
Press and release the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Within 30 seconds, press and hold the programmed HomeLink button for 2 seconds, then release.
Repeat up to 3 times until the door moves.
erase: Press and hold the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Keep holding for about 6 seconds until the LEARN LED goes out.
All remotes and keypads are now erased; reprogram the ones you want to keep.

car: Program the HomeLink button with your remote first (see your vehicle's steps).
Press and release the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Within 30 seconds, press and hold the programmed HomeLink button for 2 seconds, then release.
Repeat up to 3 times until the door moves.
erase: Press and hold the LEARN button on the opener motor unit.
Keep holding for about 6 seconds until the LEARN LED goes out.
All remotes and keypads are now erased; reprogram the ones you want to keep.

openers.learn_button_location: On the powerhead: a square PROGRAM/SET button next to the round and long LEDs.

remote: Find the square PROGRAM/SET (PRGM) button on the opener powerhead.

Repeat for each extra button or remote.
keypad: Make sure the keypad's backlight is off.

Press the UP/DOWN key slowly 3–4 times until the opener runs.
car: Clear the HomeLink buttons first by holding the 1st and 3rd buttons until the indicator flashes fast (about 20 seconds).

Press and hold the UP and DOWN buttons together until both LEDs turn blue.

Press and hold the remote button, then also press and hold the HomeLink button.
Keep both held until the HomeLink indicator flashes slowly then quickly; release.
Put the opener in programming mode (hold PROGRAM/SET until blue, then release).
Press the HomeLink button for 2 seconds, release, and repeat until the door moves.
erase: Hold PROGRAM/SET until the round LED turns blue, then release (long LED flashes purple).
Press and hold the UP and DOWN buttons together until both LEDs turn blue.

Hold the garage door remote 1–3 in away from the HomeLink buttons on the inside rear-view mirror.
Press and hold the HomeLink button you want to use and the remote's button together.
Keep holding until the HomeLink indicator starts flashing quickly (or stays lit), then let go.
Press the HomeLink button. If the door moves, programming is done; if not, follow the rolling-code steps.
rolling_code_steps: Find the Learn (or Smart) button on the garage door opener motor; a ladder may be needed.
Press and release the Learn button; you then have about 30 seconds.
Return to the vehicle and press and hold the programmed HomeLink button for 2 seconds, then release.
Repeat the press-hold-release up to 3 times until the door moves.
cars.rolling_code_note: Openers made after about 1995 usually use rolling codes and need the Learn-button step.

Hold the garage door remote 1–3 in away from the HomeLink buttons on the inside rear-view mirror.
Press and hold the HomeLink button you want to use and the remote's button together.
Keep holding until the HomeLink indicator starts flashing quickly (or stays lit), then let go.
Press the HomeLink button. If the door moves, programming is done; if not, follow the rolling-code steps.
rolling_code_steps: Find the Learn (or Smart) button on the garage door opener motor; a ladder may be needed.
Press and release the Learn button; you then have about 60 seconds.
Return to the vehicle and press and hold the programmed HomeLink button for 2 seconds, then release.
Repeat the press-hold-release up to 3 times until the door moves.
erase_steps: Press and hold the two outer HomeLink buttons for about 10 seconds.
Release when the indicator light changes; all three buttons are now cleared.
cars.rolling_code_note: Openers made after about 1995 usually use rolling codes and need the Learn-button step.

Return to the vehicle and press and hold the programmed HomeLink button for 2 seconds, then release.
Repeat the press-hold-release up to 3 times until the door moves.
cars.rolling_code_note: Openers made after about 1995 usually use rolling codes and need the Learn-button step.

steps: Park outside the garage with the vehicle switched on and keep people and objects clear of the door.
Hold the garage door remote 1–3 in away from the HomeLink buttons on the inside rear-view mirror.
Press and hold the HomeLink button you want to use and the remote's button together.
Keep holding until the HomeLink indicator starts flashing quickly (or stays lit), then let go.
Press the HomeLink button. If the door moves, programming is done; if not, follow the rolling-code steps.

Hold the garage door remote 1–3 in away from the HomeLink buttons on the inside rear-view mirror.
Press and hold the HomeLink button you want to use and the remote's button together.
Keep holding until the HomeLink indicator starts flashing quickly (or stays lit), then let go.
Press the HomeLink button. If the door moves, programming is done; if not, follow the rolling-code steps.
rolling_code_steps: Find the Learn (or Smart) button on the garage door opener motor; a ladder may be needed.
Press and release the Learn button; you then have about 60 seconds.
Return to the vehicle and press and hold the programmed HomeLink button for 2 seconds, then release.
Repeat the press-hold-release up to 3 times until the door moves.
erase_steps: Press and hold the two outer HomeLink buttons for about 10 seconds.
Release when the indicator light changes; all three buttons are now cleared.
cars.rolling_code_note: Openers made after about 1995 usually use rolling codes and need the Learn-button step.
